name: Ocher Red
lede: Ocher red is the red of iron oxide earth: the oldest pigment family, dug from the ground or made by roasting yellow ochre, and used in painting for a very long time.

sections.title: What the pigment is
sections.body:
The coloring matter in red ochre is hematite, an iron oxide with the formula Fe2O3, in very fine grains [1]. Ochres are secondary deposits, found as soils or as gossans, the weathered and oxidized surface of ore bodies, enriched in iron oxides or hydroxides [1]. Their colors are strong and permanent [1].

Yellow ochre turns red when heated, which was known in the Palaeolithic period [2]. The result is sold as burnt ochre, a process the Pigment Compendium calls the first synthetic pigment [2]. See [[ochre]] for the yellow side of the family, and [[venetian-red]] for the synthetic relative [1].

sections.title: One pigment, many names
sections.body:
Church's list of synonyms for red earth pigments runs from red haematite and red iron ore to scarlet ochre, red chalk, *sinopis*, *rubrica*, *miltos*, *terra rosa* and Arrabida red [3]. Armenian bole is a related deep red ochre first found in Cappadocia [3]. Pliny, writing in the first century, says yellow ochre was also dug in hills about 20 miles from Rome and then burnt, and that some sellers adulterated it and passed it off as dark ochre [4].

The phrase "ochre-red" also appears as a plain color description. Salter in 1869 calls the color of silver chromate a fine ochre-red [5].

sections.title: In use
sections.body:
The mineral pigments on Greek and Roman statuary included yellow ochre, red ochre, cinnabar and hematite, among others [6]. In Shakespeare's time painters of Stratford coloured cloth hangings with ochre reds and yellows, lime white and soot [7]. In Aboriginal Australia, Finlay realized that the natural dye colors of a bag mirror the ochres: red, white, yellow and black [8].

The cheap earth also served as a cheat. Salter lists red ochre among the adulterants of ground madder root, along with brickdust and sawdust [9]. Ground [[irresistible]] was worth much more than the red earth it was cut with [9].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
The swatch measures a lightness of 50 and a chroma of about 31, with a hue angle of 37 degrees, a brownish red [10]. Its contrast ratio against white is 4.5 to 1 [10]. The nearest named colors are Etruscan Red at about 3 units, Hydrangea Red at about 5, and Pinkish Brown, Redwood and Copper Penny at 5 to 6 [10].

We have no archive count, and a color match in a painting is not a pigment test. Screen colors are approximate [10].
